title: Make, Communicate & Verify a Decision
summary: Learn how to make a reasoned decision, explain why it was chosen, communicate responsibilities, and verify whether the decision produced the intended result.
objectives: Choose an option using evidence and decision criteria.
Communicate a decision, rationale, ownership, and next steps clearly.
Define how the result of a decision will be checked.

vocab.def: A selected course of action after considering available information and options.
The reasoning that explains why a decision was made.
Checking whether an action or decision produced the expected result.
Specific conditions used to determine whether a result is acceptable.

sections.heading: A decision should connect to the evidence
sections.body: Strong decisions can be explained. The selected option should connect to the problem, available evidence, relevant constraints, and the criteria used to compare alternatives.

sections.heading: Communicate what happens next
sections.body: A decision is incomplete if nobody knows who is responsible, what action is expected, when it should happen, or what conditions could require reconsideration.

sections.heading: Explain the rationale
sections.body: Sharing the reasoning behind a decision helps others understand the tradeoffs and assumptions that shaped it. This can also make future review easier.

sections.heading: Verify the result
sections.body: Do not assume that taking action means the problem is solved. Define what result should be observed and check whether that result actually occurred.

practice.prompt: A team implements a solution and immediately closes the issue without checking the result. What problem-solving step is missing?
You make a decision that affects several coworkers. What should be communicated?
practice.answer: The decision, rationale when appropriate, responsible owner, expected actions, timing, and how the result will be checked.

quiz.question: Why should a workplace decision include verification?
options: To determine whether the action produced the intended result
To prove the original decision could never be wrong
To eliminate the need for future communication
quiz.answer: To determine whether the action produced the intended result

lab.objective: Choose an option from a simulated problem, document the rationale, assign next steps, and define measurable or observable success criteria.

reflectionPrompt: Why is taking action different from proving that a problem has actually been solved?

proofActivity.title: Prove: workplace problem solving
proofActivity.description: Use the available facts and constraints to define the workplace problem, compare reasonable options, select a next step, and explain how the result should be verified.
criteria: Defines the workplace problem using relevant facts
Selects and explains an appropriate next step
Defines a verification or follow-up method

prompts.uncertainty: What remains uncertain or could change the decision?
